source.title: Reasoned Safety Alignment: Ensuring Jailbreak Defense via Answer-Then-Check
source.authors: Chen-Tao Cao; Xiaojun Xu; Bo Han; Hang Li

record.file_problem: The text contains the full paper and appendices. Some tables are flattened, and the opening includes stray text, but these do not prevent extracting the reported prefilling and GCG results.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly evaluates prefilling and adversarial-suffix attacks against safety-trained models. Its results refine or challenge the claim that getting past the opening defeats safety: the tested ReSA models retain high reported safety scores under these attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, safety localization in weights, or safety erosion from fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples. Its general safety tables and training-size ablations concern the performance of the proposed safety-training method, not those claim versions. Rows below are limited to reported prefilling and GCG attack results.
record.test_reason: This is a defense-method paper. Its appendix attack results bear on V4: a GCG suffix targeting 'Sure' (Table 11) and a prefilled fake 'approved' safety check (Table 13), both on safety-trained models. The base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct under GCG is a direct V4 data point. The prefilling and ReSA-SFT GCG results show where the bypass fails, for models trained to decide on safety after an answer summary. The study is not an original source. It does not replicate the original prefill-harmful-tokens setup, so T3 fits rather than T1 or T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that ReSA-SFT stays robust to prefilling: most conditions are essentially unchanged, PAIR-GPT drops, and the average falls by 3.68 points (0.9633→0.9265). They propose rule-based rejection of queries containing special tokens as a further defense. Under GCG, ReSA-SFT beats the base model and WJ-SFT. It is slightly below STAIR-DPO on the StrongREJECT and HarmBench evaluators, which the authors attribute to STAIR-DPO's extra DPO stage.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains ReSA models with Answer-Then-Check SFT and RL; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning compromise or per-token KL methods. Prefilling and GCG are used to evaluate attack robustness.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefilling results vary by jailbreak prompt type: the PAIR-GPT condition has a larger reported decline than None, PAP, or DeepInception.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the attack results. The prefilling evaluation is for ReSA-SFT on one base model and uses the study's particular structured prefill, not a generic few-token opening. The GCG result uses 50 prompts and one stated target-string strategy. The study reports evaluator-scored safety measures rather than a direct harmful-completion rate.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were left out from the directly relevant prefilling and GCG evaluations. Other jailbreak attack results were not extracted because the listed claim versions do not specifically cover those attacks.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning attack on safety-trained models.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis of aligned versus base models.

No prefilling of harmful response tokens on standard instruct models. No decoding-change attacks. Prefilling was applied only to ReSA-SFT (Llama3.1-8B). GCG was run only on Qwen2.5-7B-based models with 50 prompts.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.
No measurement of whether ReSA spreads safety beyond the first tokens. Its robustness to prefilling is relevant only indirectly.

missing.what: Base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct under GCG: LlamaGuard DSR 0.62, StrongREJECT goodness 0.5727, HarmBench DSR 0.58. This is the direct V4 result on a standard safety-trained model and should be a main row.
WJ-SFT (0.76/0.8150/0.84) and STAIR-DPO (0.98/0.9937/1.0) under GCG on Qwen2.5-7B / Qwen2-7B. These show the GCG bypass varies by safety training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label is too strong. The robust results come from the study's own defense model, which is trained to make its safety decision after an answer summary. That makes them a scope condition on V4, not evidence that V4 fails for ordinary aligned models. The only standard-model V4 evidence (base Qwen under GCG) shows partial bypass. The prefill tested is the study's own template (an empty summary plus 'Therefore, I can provide this answer'), not harmful-content tokens. GCG uses 50 prompts, while the unattacked values cover 313 prompts, so the baselines are not matched. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether harmful fine-tuning examples remove refusal.
The study does not test whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning data raises harmful compliance.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is reported.

Tests prefilling a structured compliant opening and a GCG adversarial suffix targeting “Sure”; it does not test decoding changes or whether a few compliant tokens alone raise harmful-completion rates.
No weight or rank localization of safety behaviour is tested.
The study does not test whether data or a training objective produces shallow safety.
The study does not measure whether safety training spreads beyond the first response tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct under a GCG suffix targeting 'Sure', 50 StrongREJECT prompts
relationships.reason: Taken from the text, not a row (see missing). DSR falls to 0.62, 0.57 and 0.58 across the three evaluators (Table 11), against roughly 0.97 unattacked on the full set. This is a substantial but incomplete bypass. R5-R7 record these values only as baselines.
relationships.display_finding: The defense success rate fell to 0.62, 0.57 and 0.58 across three evaluators, against roughly 0.97 unattacked on the full set, a substantial but incomplete bypass.

relationships.condition: ReSA-SFT (Answer-Then-Check trained) Llama3.1-8B with a prefilled fake approved safety check, on None/PAP/DeepInception prompts
relationships.reason: DSR changes by at most 0.016 under the prefill (R1, R3, R4). Models trained to check an answer summary before replying mostly resist an opening that bypasses the check.
relationships.display_finding: Defense success changed by at most 0.016 under the prefill, so the trained model mostly resisted an opening that skips its safety check.
